metrics.method: Full history 2026-03-23 to 2026-09-17, 883 records (864 messages + 19 service events). Client side = alias 'Vale' from config/clients.yaml; all 9 other senders (Fredo, Ollie Mckinlay, Stephski, Mayson Chat, Michelle Queue, Mica Vecco, Derrek, Eric The Efficient, Vivek) resolve to config/team.yaml, so there is no vendor chat team on this account. client_questions_total = client messages containing '?' (57). unanswered_over_24h = distinct client questions/requests with no SUBSTANTIVE answer inside 24h, read by hand (12); 8 of those have never been answered at all: 'Should I change my password?' (Jul 28, 52d), 'Anything I should know before the live ? / How many minutes and what he wants ?' (Aug 3), 'Was a call booked for today ?' (Aug 7), 'Can you guys tell me what you have on him on your notes ?' (Aug 7, 42d), which of her two Snapchat accounts we want admin on (Sep 10, 8d), what the recurring OnlyFans alerts actually are (first screenshotted Aug 29, 20d), her Facebook answer 'I have my one with my family members and old friends' (Sep 16), and the three uncaptioned photos posted into the OnlyFans topic on Sep 17 (ids 886/887/888). The purely mechanical count (any team message within 24h of a client burst) is 8 of 164 bursts, which understates the problem: we are almost always in the room, we just do not answer. Median lag from the start of a client burst to the next team message is 0.23h across 164 bursts (p75 5.7h, p90 19h). max_team_silence_days = longest gap between consecutive messages from our side = 5.2d (May 5 -> May 10); the longest stretch with no NON-templated outbound is 8.9d (Aug 20 -> Aug 29, broken only by an automated leak report). promises_made counts explicit forward-looking commitments by our side ('I'll send X', 'we can get them scheduled', a booked call, a stated cadence such as 'biweekly call' or 'creative ideas weekly'); kept = evidence of delivery in-chat; lapsed = no delivery and no further mention; the remaining 4 are pending or unverifiable from the log.

top_fix: Make closing a loop in writing someone's actual job on this account — a standing, dated close-out posted into the client chat every week by the account lead: every paid fan order (delivered / booked for X / not started), every promise made in the chat, one OnlyFans performance number, and one line confirming each payment has been SEEN in the bank. Nothing here failed for lack of contact — five of our people appeared in the last week alone and our median reply is 14 minutes. It failed because no commitment on this account has ever had a required end-state, so 28 promises lapsed silently, $5,300 of fan money sits undelivered for up to 166 days, three consecutive payments are unreconciled, a $2,000 custom was found by accident three months late, and her 52-day-old security question is still open. A weekly written ledger would have caught every one of those before the client did — and it is the only thing that would have turned 'you won’t lose your account' from a reassurance into a control on an account she has already lost once.
